topic.name: Phase Portraits for Decoupled Linear Systems

question.text: Consider the phase portrait for a decoupled system above. Which of the following systems could correspond to the given portrait?
question.explanation:
Writing a decoupled system in matrix form, we have \[ \mathbf{x}'(t) = \begin{bmatrix} \lambda_1 & 0 \\ 0 & \lambda_2 \end{bmatrix} \mathbf{x}(t) \] where $\mathbf x(t) = \begin{bmatrix} x(t)\\y(t)\end{bmatrix}.$

Since our system is decoupled, its eigenvectors are parallel to the axes. These correspond to so-called straight-line solutions of the form \[ c_1 e^{\lambda_1 t} \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} \qquad\text{and}\qquad c_2 e^{\lambda_2 t} \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

Now, notice that:

  • The tangents along the $x$-axis are pointing away from the origin, meaning that the solutions of the form $ c_1 e^{\lambda_1 t} \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} $ must approach infinity as $t \to \infty.$ So, we must have $\lambda_1 > 0.$

  • The tangents along the $y$-axis are pointing toward the origin, meaning that the solutions of the form $ c_2 e^{\lambda_2 t} \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} $ must approach the origin as $t \to \infty.$ So, we must have $\lambda_2 < 0.$

Among the options, the only system that satisfies $\lambda_1 > 0$ and $\lambda_2 < 0$ is the following: \[ \begin{cases} x'(t) = 2x(t) \\[3pt] y'(t) = -3y(t) \end{cases} \]

question.text: \[ \begin{cases} x'(t) = -5x(t) \\[3pt] y'(t) = -3y(t) \end{cases} \] Which of the following could represent the phase portrait of the decoupled system above?
question.explanation:
Writing our system in matrix form, we have \[ \mathbf{x}'(t) = \begin{bmatrix} -5 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 \end{bmatrix} \mathbf{x}(t) \] where $\mathbf x(t) = \begin{bmatrix} x(t)\\ y(t)\end{bmatrix}.$

Since our system is decoupled, its eigenvectors are the following:

  • Eigenvalue $\lambda_1=-5$ with the corresponding eigenvector $\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}.$

  • Eigenvalue $\lambda_2=-3$ with the corresponding eigenvector $\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.$

The general solution of the system is \[ \mathbf{x}(t) = c_1 e^{-5t} \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} + c_2 e^{-3 t} \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}. \]

Now, notice that:

  • The straight-line solutions of the form $ c_1 e^{-5t} \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} $ lie on the $x$-axis. Since $e^{-t} \to 0$ as $t \to \infty,$ these solutions approach the origin as $t \to \infty.$

  • The straight-line solutions of the form $ c_2 e^{-3 t} \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} $ lie on the $y$-axis. Since $e^{-3t} \to 0$ as $t \to \infty,$ these solutions also approach the origin as $t \to \infty.$

Among the given options, there are two phase portraits satisfying these conditions:

Let's consider the solutions $x(t) = c_1e^{-5t}$ and $y(t)=c_2e^{-3t}$ provided that $c_1,c_2 \neq 0.$ Then,

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} = \dfrac{y'(t)}{x'(t)} = \dfrac{(c_2e^{-3t})'}{(c_1e^{-5t})'} = \dfrac{-3c_2e^{-3t}}{-5c_1e^{-5t}} = \dfrac{3c_2}{5c_1}e^{2t}. \end{align*}

example.title: Identifying the Phase Portrait Given a System: Advanced Cases

question.text: \[ \begin{cases} x'(t) = -4x(t) \\[3pt] y'(t) = -5y(t) \end{cases} \] Select the correct options below regarding the given decoupled system of linear differential equations.
question.explanation:
Writing our system in matrix form, we have \[ \mathbf{x}'(t) = \begin{bmatrix} -4 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 \end{bmatrix} \mathbf{x}(t) \] where $\mathbf x(t) = \begin{bmatrix} x(t)\\ y(t)\end{bmatrix}.$

Recall that a homogeneous system of linear differential equations has a single equilibrium (fixed point) at the origin.

Since our system is decoupled, its eigenvectors are the following:

  • Eigenvalue $\lambda_1=-4$ with the eigenvector $\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}.$ The corresponding straight-line solutions of the form $ c_1 e^{-4t} \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} $ lie on the $x$-axis and approach the origin as $t \to \infty.$ So, the $x$-axis is the $\bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{\text{stable}}$ line.

  • Eigenvalue $\lambda_2=-5$ with the eigenvector $\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.$ The corresponding straight-line solutions of the form $ c_2 e^{-5t} \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} $ lie on the $y$-axis and also approach the origin as $t \to \infty.$ So, the $y$-axis is the $\bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{\text{stable}}$ line.

Therefore, the equilibrium point (origin) is $\bbox[4pt, border: solid 1pt gainsboro]{\text{a stable node (sink)}}.$
